why: The Terminal wire, which has two writers and no registration step: `control/orchestrator/src/panels/types.ts` declares the shape the streamer serialises, and `cli/panels.go` declares a Go struct whose `json:"..."` tags decode it. Neither file imports the other and neither is generated from the other, so the only thing keeping the two key sets equal is that somebody remembered.
failure: A KEY THAT DRIFTS DECODES TO THE ZERO VALUE, WHICH IS A BLANK CELL, WHICH READS AS DATA. `encoding/json` ignores keys it was not told about and leaves fields it was not given untouched — it does not error, and there is no strict mode in this path. So a renamed key produces a column of `-` in `kontra panels`, and `dashIfEmpty` renders that identically to a Machine that genuinely has no Fleet. Both halves keep passing their own tests: the TypeScript tests assert the TypeScript spelling, and the Go tests build their fixtures FROM the Go struct, so each side agrees with itself all the way to green.
history:
Swept 2026-08-30, during the retirement of the word `campaign`. Two live drifts were sitting in this one struct:
  * `campaign` -> `fleet`. types.ts renamed the key (its comment even records the rename: "Was `campaign`") and panels.go kept asking for `campaign`. Every Terminal in `kontra panels` had rendered `-` in that column since the rename, on every Fleet.
  * `role`. panels.go declared `Role string `json:"role"``; the streamer has never emitted `role` — its key is `tag` — and no Go line ever read `.Role`. A field decoding nothing into a value nobody used.
Neither had a failing test on either side. This is ADR 0035 rule two, and the repo had already paid for the same shape once when the Batch content hash was pinned by a hand-copied golden and the two SDKs hashed one Batch to different keys for months.

keys.why: The contract is the SPELLING, not the values. A driver on each side asserts that its own declaration carries exactly these keys — so a rename in either file fails a test in the OTHER language, which is the only arrangement that makes a one-sided rename impossible.
keys.containment: The two arms assert DIFFERENT things, and the asymmetry is the design. TypeScript is the WRITER: its interface must carry exactly `required` + `optional`, no more and no less, because a key it stops sending is a key some reader is still waiting for. Go is a READER: its declared tags must be a SUBSET of `required` + `optional`, because ignoring a key is correct and common — this command has no column for `command`, `paneCols`, `paneRows` or `telemetry` and should not grow fields for them — while declaring a key nobody sends is the silent-blank bug.

notes.mode: Sent `omitempty` from Go and optional in TS ON PURPOSE — an older streamer sends no `mode` at all and its ids still carry one, so `modeName` falls back to the id prefix rather than blanking the column. Tolerance here is deliberate and is NOT the drift this corpus catches: an absent `mode` has a defined reading, a misspelled `fleet` does not.
notes.tag: The Machine tag: the cloud provider's tag, the inventory group, the `kf-<tag>-NN` name prefix. Nothing dispatches on it. NOT to be spelled `role` — the Go side declared `role` for as long as this struct existed and the streamer never sent it.
notes.fleet: Which Fleet — the stack name, `<actor>-<version>`, DERIVED from the Artifact it places. Formerly `campaign`; see `history`. The word is retired (ADR 0037), and this key is the last place it could have come back through.
notes.actor: '' when the stack carries no placement. A Machine with no actor is still a visible tile, so empty is a value here and not an absence.
notes.health: A nested object with its own writers on both sides. Its keys are NOT pinned here — `workerhealth.json` owns the health contract.

goldens.why: One serialised Terminal, so a driver can prove it round-trips rather than only that the spellings match. A key set can agree while a type does not.
goldens.note: `lastSnapshotAt` is epoch MILLISECONDS and an int64 on the Go side. It is in the golden because a seconds/millis mix-up is the other way this struct can be wrong while every spelling is right.
